two-sample-t-test.edition: Per OpenIntro Statistics Chapter 7 (inference for numerical data, Welch's t) and the Welch-Satterthwaite df, by name; the t-CDF reuses the bundled special-function helper.
two-sample-t-test.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
two-sample-t-test.editionNote: Welch's t (unequal variances); n < 2 in either group is rejected. Small n (< 30) - the normality assumption applies.

assumptions.name: Welch's t
assumptions.value: does not assume equal variances; uses the Welch-Satterthwaite df

tapered-flocculation-g.formula: P_stage = G_stage^2 x mu(T) x V_stage (Camp-Stein inverted); Gt = mean(G) x total_time; mu = water dynamic viscosity at the given temperature.
tapered-flocculation-g.edition: Camp-Stein velocity gradient, tapered multi-stage schedule (Camp & Stein 1943; Ten States Standards), by name.
tapered-flocculation-g.freeAccess: The velocity-gradient relation is a public water-treatment result; the viscosity comes from a standard water-property table and the treatment-process design governs.
tapered-flocculation-g.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
tapered-flocculation-g.editionNote: A tapered schedule decreases G stage to stage - the vigorous first stage builds many small flocs and each gentler stage grows them without the shear that would tear them apart; each stage should sit in the 10-100 per-second flocculation band (rapid mix, G of at least 750 per Ten States, belongs in a separate basin). Cold water is more viscous, so the same G costs more power in winter. Gt characterizes the whole train (10^4-10^5 typical). A design aid, not a process design.

assumptions.name: Equal stages
assumptions.value: each stage is taken at the same volume; the power is P = G^2 mu V per stage from the inverted Camp-Stein relation

assumptions.name: Tapered band
assumptions.value: G decreases stage to stage, each in the 10-100/s flocculation band; merging rapid mix shears the floc

chimney-draft.formula: T_o_R = ambient_temp_f + 460; T_m_R = mean_flue_temp_f + 460; D_t = 0.52 x baro_psia x stack_height_ft x (1/T_o_R - 1/T_m_R) [in wc]; D_net = net_factor x D_t.
chimney-draft.edition: ASHRAE Handbook HVAC Systems (chimney/vent) / NFPA 211 theoretical chimney draft, by name.
chimney-draft.freeAccess: The theoretical-draft relation is standard chimney/vent design practice; the venting standard and appliance instructions govern the actual sign-off.
chimney-draft.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
chimney-draft.editionNote: This is the theoretical no-flow draft, so the net available after flow and fitting losses is far lower (apply about 0.5 to 0.8). The barometric pressure must be altitude-corrected because thinner air at elevation cuts the draft. The temperatures must be absolute (Rankine), and T_m is the mean flue temperature, not the outlet. The venting standard (NFPA 211) and the appliance instructions govern - a design aid, not a venting sign-off.

assumptions.name: No-flow theoretical
assumptions.value: D_t is the no-flow draft; net available after flow/fitting losses is about 0.5 to 0.8 of it

assumptions.name: Altitude and absolute temps
assumptions.value: barometric pressure must be altitude-corrected; temperatures are absolute (Rankine), T_m the mean flue temp

fertigation-injection-rate.formula: total_product_gal = product_rate_gal_per_acre x area_acres; injection_rate_gph = total_product_gal / set_time_hours; injection_rate_gpm = injection_rate_gph / 60.
fertigation-injection-rate.edition: Fertigation / chemigation injection-rate practice (EPA chemigation rules; the product label under FIFRA), by name; the label, the state chemigation regulations, and a drawdown calibration govern.
fertigation-injection-rate.freeAccess: The injection-rate arithmetic is public first-principles (total product over the set time); the per-acre rate, acres, and set time come from the recommendation and the irrigation schedule.
fertigation-injection-rate.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
fertigation-injection-rate.editionNote: Fertigation (injecting fertilizer) and chemigation (injecting a pesticide or other chemical) apply a product to a field through the irrigation water rather than a sprayer. The total product needed is the recommended per-acre rate times the field acres, and to apply it uniformly it is metered in at a constant rate over the irrigation SET, so the injection-pump rate is simply the total product divided by the set duration. Applying 5 gallons per acre over 40 acres during a 6-hour set is 200 gallons total, injected at 33.3 gallons per hour (about 0.56 gpm). Operationally the injection is started only after the irrigation system has come up to pressure and the most distant emitter or sprinkler is flowing (so the whole field receives product), and the lines are flushed with clear water at the end of the set to clear the chemical. When the product is a stock or concentrate solution, its resulting concentration in the irrigation water is the injection flow divided by the system flow multiplied by the stock strength, which sets the dilution needed to hit a target ppm, and a tank-mixed formulation is checked for compatibility before it is injected. A critical regulatory point: whenever a chemical is injected, an EPA-required, functioning backflow-prevention package -- an anti-siphon device, a check valve, a low-pressure drain, and an interlock that shuts the injection pump off if the irrigation pump stops -- must protect the water source, and the actual injection rate is calibrated against a drawdown (or weight) check on the day of application. A rate estimate; the product label (which is enforceable law under FIFRA), the state chemigation regulations, and the applicator's calibration govern.

assumptions.name: Injection rate
assumptions.value: total product = rate (gal/acre) x acres; injection rate = total / set time; stock ppm = (injection flow/system flow) x stock strength

assumptions.name: Backflow protection + calibration
assumptions.value: an EPA-required anti-siphon/check-valve/interlock package must protect the water source; calibrate against a drawdown check; the FIFRA label and state chemigation rules govern

parallel-conductor-derate.formula: I_total = I_single x N x F_ccc x F_ambient, where N is the number of identical parallel sets, F_ccc is the more-than-three current-carrying-conductor adjustment (1.0 for <=3, 0.8 for 4-6, 0.7 for 7-9, 0.5 for 10-20, ...), and F_ambient the temperature correction. Per-set current I_set = I_load / N. Paralleling is permitted only at 1/0 AWG and larger.
parallel-conductor-derate.edition: NEC (NFPA 70) Article 310 paralleled-conductor provisions and the 310.15(C)(1) adjustment factors, by name.
parallel-conductor-derate.freeAccess: NFPA 70 free read-only at nfpa.org/freeaccess; conductor ampacities user-supplied from the adopted edition's ampacity table.
parallel-conductor-derate.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
parallel-conductor-derate.editionNote: AHJ-adopted NEC edition governs; the 1/0-AWG minimum and the all-sets-identical (length / material / termination) rule are long-standing NEC requirements.

assumptions.name: Conductor ampacity
assumptions.value: single-conductor ampacity user-supplied from the NEC ampacity table for the conductor / insulation / termination

assumptions.name: Parallel sets identical
assumptions.value: all parallel sets share length, material, size, insulation, and termination

refrigerant-velocity.formula: V_fpm = (mass_flow_lb_hr * specific_volume_ft3_lb) / area_ft2 / 60, where area = (pi/4)(ID_in/12)^2. Oil return needs a minimum velocity (higher in a suction riser); above ~4000 fpm the line is noisy.
refrigerant-velocity.edition: ASHRAE Refrigeration Handbook line-sizing and oil-return guidance, by name.
refrigerant-velocity.freeAccess: ASHRAE licensed; refrigerant specific volume is read from the manufacturer's P-T / property data (user-supplied).
refrigerant-velocity.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed mechanical contractor govern. ACCA Manual J / D / S supersede rules of thumb.
refrigerant-velocity.editionNote: Single-edition (line-velocity identity; oil-return minimums and the ~4000 fpm ceiling are advisory and manufacturer-table-governed).

assumptions.name: Oil-return window
assumptions.value: horizontal min ~700 fpm, suction-riser min ~1500 fpm, noise ceiling ~4000 fpm (advisory)

assumptions.name: Specific volume
assumptions.value: refrigerant specific volume at the line condition is strain-of-refrigerant- and state-specific and user-supplied

welded-wire-mesh.formula: effective_sheet_sf = (sheet_width_ft - side_lap_in/12) x (sheet_length_ft - end_lap_in/12); gross_area_sf = slab_area_sf x (1 + waste_pct/100); sheets = ceil(gross_area_sf / effective_sheet_sf); purchased_sf = sheets x sheet_width_ft x sheet_length_ft.
welded-wire-mesh.edition: Lapped-coverage identity by name (mesh lapped one full square); ACI / WRI (Wire Reinforcement Institute) practice; first-principles area arithmetic.
welded-wire-mesh.freeAccess: The lapped-coverage takeoff is public flatwork practice; WRI mesh-lap guidance is named.
welded-wire-mesh.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
welded-wire-mesh.editionNote: Mesh is lapped one full square (6 in minimum) at the sides and ends, so the effective coverage per sheet is less than its nominal area - ignoring the laps under-counts. The ACI / structural drawings set the sheet size and style (for example 6x6 W2.9). This is a purchase quantity, not a placement plan.

assumptions.name: Lap
assumptions.value: 6 in side and end lap default (one full square minimum); the drawings govern

assumptions.name: Sheet size
assumptions.value: 5 x 10 ft sheet default; the structural drawings set the style (e.g. 6x6 W2.9)

plywood-span.formula: Roof: allowable spacing = APA E30 Table 33 max span for the rating (with or without edge support: clips, blocking or T&G); allowable live = the Table 33 value at the next tabulated spacing at or above the actual spacing; allowable total = live + 10 psf dead. Floor: allowable spacing and total load from the rating. Pass/fail = (support_spacing ≤ allowable_spacing) AND (live_load ≤ allowable_live) AND (live + dead ≤ allowable_total).
plywood-span.edition: APA - The Engineered Wood Association published span-rating tables by name. Cited by APA name only; numeric tables shipped under APA's technical-bulletin reuse policy. IRC 2021 (International Residential Code). §R503 / §R803 references the APA tables.
plywood-span.freeAccess: APA technical bulletins free at apawood.org/publications.
plywood-span.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed structural engineer govern.
plywood-span.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow IRC 2021. Jurisdictions on IRC 2018 / 2024 differ at the margins; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ. APA span-rating values are stable across editions.

assumptions.name: Span-rating table
assumptions.value: data/construction/apa-span-ratings.json keyed to rating × application

boiler-pipe-sizing.formula: GPM = Q / (500 × delta-T) (hydronic water energy balance). Velocity (ft/s) = GPM / (2.448 × d_in²). The smallest standard inner diameter whose velocity is at or below the ceiling is recommended. Head loss = Hazen-Williams (C = 150 copper/PEX, 130 steel); pump head = head per 100 ft × run length / 100.
boiler-pipe-sizing.edition: ASHRAE Systems and Equipment 2020 Chapter 13 (hydronic heating) by name; Bell & Gossett / Taco system-design velocity limits by name. Hazen-Williams (1905) public domain.
boiler-pipe-sizing.freeAccess: ASHRAE Handbook TOC free at ashrae.org; B&G / Taco design guides free at bellgossett.com / tacocomfort.com.
boiler-pipe-sizing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed mechanical contractor govern. ACCA Manual J / D / S supersede rules of thumb.
boiler-pipe-sizing.editionNote: Standard inner diameters: copper Type L (ASTM B88), steel Schedule 40 (ASTM A53), PEX SDR-9 (ASTM F876). Default velocity ceilings 4 ft/s copper, 6 ft/s steel, 3 ft/s PEX; fitting equivalent length is added separately for the final pump head.

assumptions.name: Water factor
assumptions.value: 500 BTU/(hr · gpm · °F)
assumptions.source: 60 min/hr × 8.33 lb/gal × 1 BTU/lb-°F (physical fact for water)

assumptions.name: Hazen-Williams C
assumptions.value: 150 copper / PEX, 130 black steel

assumptions.name: Default velocity ceiling
assumptions.value: 4 / 6 / 3 ft/s (copper / steel / PEX)

assumptions.name: Water near room temperature
assumptions.value: Hazen-Williams is an empirical fit for cool water; hot hydronic water is less viscous, so the head loss shown runs high (conservative), and it does not apply to glycol solutions, whose heat capacity also changes the 500 factor

compressor-short-cycle.formula: Cycle rate N = N_max × 4 × X × (1 − X), where X is the runtime (load) fraction and N_max is the per-hour ceiling; the parabola peaks at X = 0.5. On-time = X × 60 / N; off-time = (1 − X) × 60 / N. Short-cycling is flagged when the estimated on-time is below the minimum oil-return runtime or the observed cycles exceed the ceiling.
compressor-short-cycle.edition: Copeland Application Engineering Bulletin 17-1226 by name; ASHRAE Fundamentals 2021. The ASHRAE/AHRI part-load cycling model by name.
compressor-short-cycle.freeAccess: Copeland AE bulletins free at copeland.com/literature; ASHRAE Handbook TOC free at ashrae.org.
compressor-short-cycle.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed mechanical contractor govern. ACCA Manual J / D / S supersede rules of thumb.
compressor-short-cycle.editionNote: Thresholds: single-stage 10-min on / 5-min off / 6 cph; two-stage 8 / 5 / 8; VRF / inverter modulate capacity (4-min on, per-manufacturer, no fixed cycles-per-hour ceiling). Per-manufacturer guidance governs final operation.

assumptions.name: Cycling parabola
assumptions.value: N = N_max × 4 × X × (1 − X)

assumptions.name: Single-stage minimum runtime
assumptions.value: 10 min on, 5 min off
assumptions.source: Copeland AE Bulletin 17-1226 / industry rule of thumb

assumptions.name: Cycles-per-hour ceiling
assumptions.value: 6 single-stage, 8 two-stage

septic-lpp-orifice.formula: Per-orifice flow (gpm) = 19.63 x Cd x d_in^2 x sqrt(h_ft) (Cd 0.6 gives the familiar 11.79 coefficient); system flow = per-orifice flow x orifices per lateral x laterals.
septic-lpp-orifice.edition: Standard orifice-discharge equation; university onsite-wastewater extension low-pressure-pipe design guidance, by name.
septic-lpp-orifice.freeAccess: Extension LPP design guidance free on land-grant university extension sites.
septic-lpp-orifice.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed plumber / gas fitter govern. Verify against the IPC / IFGC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
septic-lpp-orifice.editionNote: Single-edition (orifice-discharge equation + extension LPP design guidance).

assumptions.name: Discharge coefficient
assumptions.value: Cd 0.6 default (gives the 11.79 / 19.63x0.6 orifice coefficient); editable

assumptions.name: Squirt height target
assumptions.value: roughly 2.5 to 5 ft (about 1 to 2 psi) for LPP, higher for mound or drip

assumptions.name: Ten-percent rule
assumptions.value: a uniform squirt requires distal-to-proximal flow to vary by less than about 10%; orifice size, spacing, and layout come from the permitted onsite design

stormwater-rational.formula: Q = C × i × A. C from bundled runoff coefficients per surface; i from user-supplied design rainfall intensity; A in acres yields Q in cfs (1 cfs ≈ 449 gpm).
stormwater-rational.edition: Rational method by name (public hydrology). C-values from public engineering practice.
stormwater-rational.freeAccess: Rainfall intensity / IDF curves free at hdsc.nws.noaa.gov (NOAA Atlas 14).
stormwater-rational.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed plumber / gas fitter govern. Verify against the IPC / IFGC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.

assumptions.name: C-values
assumptions.value: data/plumbing/runoff-coefficients.json keyed to surface

assumptions.name: Time of concentration
assumptions.value: user-supplied; method assumes Q peaks at Tc

inspection-checklist.formula: (reference page; no compute) Per-trade rough-in and final inspection checklists organized by inspection point: electrical (NEC 2023), plumbing (IPC 2021), mechanical (IMC 2021), and structural framing (IRC 2021).
inspection-checklist.edition: NEC 2023 (NFPA 70). IPC 2021 (International Plumbing Code). IMC 2021. IRC 2021. All cited by section number only.
inspection-checklist.freeAccess: Free read-only access at nfpa.org/freeaccess. IPC / IMC / IRC: Free read-only access at codes.iccsafe.org.
inspection-checklist.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
inspection-checklist.editionNote: Editions available: NEC 2023, IPC 2021, IMC 2021, IRC 2021. Inspection points are stable across recent editions; section numbering may shift.

bolt-stretch.formula: Clamp load F = (stretch × area × E) / grip. Stretch is residual elongation after torque; E is fastener elastic modulus per material.
bolt-stretch.edition: ASTM A325 / A490 / SAE J429 by name; SAE bolt material moduli (steel ~ 30e6 psi, stainless A2/A4 ~ 28e6, Inconel 718 ~ 29.6e6, titanium 6Al-4V ~ 16.5e6, aluminum 2024 ~ 10.6e6). The code uses these except Inconel 31e6 and aluminum 10e6, round figures within the grade-to-grade spread; enter the fastener maker's modulus for a critical joint.
bolt-stretch.freeAccess: ASTM / SAE licensed; engineering-property values free in Machinery's Handbook (older editions free at archive.org).
bolt-stretch.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.

assumptions.name: Elastic-region behavior
assumptions.value: true (stretch < proof-load yield)

keg-yield.formula: gross_oz = gallons x 128; net_oz = gross_oz x (1 - loss_fraction); servings = net_oz / serving_oz; cost_per_serving = keg_cost / servings; pour_cost_pct = cost_per_serving / menu_price x 100.
keg-yield.edition: Published US keg volumes (half barrel 15.5 gal, quarter barrel 7.75 gal, sixth barrel 5.16 gal, full barrel 31 gal) and the 128 fluid ounces per US gallon, by name, with a draft-system loss fraction from public bar-operations practice; the bar's own measured yield over several kegs governs.
keg-yield.freeAccess: Keg volumes and the gallon-to-ounce conversion are public. The loss fraction, keg cost, serving size, and menu price are the bar's own values.
keg-yield.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
keg-yield.editionNote: A half barrel is 15.5 gallons, which is 1,984 fluid ounces, which on paper is 124 sixteen-ounce pints, and no bar gets 124. Foam at the tap, the first pull off a fresh keg, line cleaning, the heel left behind, and the head on every glass take 10% to 20% off the top, and a poorly balanced draft system takes considerably more. The point of the calculation is that pour cost has to be computed against the net yield rather than the gross one; pricing off the paper number understates the cost of every pint by the whole loss fraction. Because the loss is a system property rather than a purchasing one, it is also the cheapest thing to fix: tightening a system from a 15% loss to an 8% loss adds roughly nine pints to a half barrel and moves the pour cost by a point and a half without touching the menu price. The catalog's draft beer line balancing tile is where that work happens, and its pour-cost tile prices a drink once the cost per ounce is known; this one produces that cost per ounce from the keg. An operating estimate; the bar's own measured yield over several kegs governs.

assumptions.name: Keg volumes
assumptions.value: half barrel 15.5 gal, quarter barrel 7.75 gal, sixth barrel 5.16 gal, full barrel 31 gal; 128 fl oz per gallon

assumptions.name: Loss fraction
assumptions.value: 10% to 20% for a working draft system; higher when the system is out of balance

assumptions.name: Net, not gross
assumptions.value: pour cost must be computed against net ounces; the gross figure understates the cost of every serving

tractor-ballast.formula: target_weight_lb = weight_to_power_ratio x power_hp; ballast_change_lb = target_weight_lb - current_weight_lb (positive = add, negative = remove).
tractor-ballast.edition: ASABE tractor-ballasting guidance (Agricultural Machinery Management) and the operator's manual, by name; the ratio, front/rear split, and tire ratings come from the manual.
tractor-ballast.freeAccess: The ballast identity is a first-principles product (ratio x power); the weight-to-power ratio target and the current weight are user-supplied from ASABE guidance and the scale.
tractor-ballast.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
tractor-ballast.editionNote: Ballast a tractor to a target total weight = weight-to-power ratio x power. ASABE and operator-manual rules of thumb: about 120 to 145 lb/hp for tillage and drawbar work at field speeds, dropping toward 90 to 110 lb/hp for higher-speed transport and lighter draft. The target is 8 to 15% wheel slip -- too much ballast wastes fuel to rolling resistance, too little spins the tires and wastes power. A positive result is ballast to ADD; a negative result is ballast to REMOVE. The ratio, the front-to-rear split, the tire load and inflation ratings, and MFWD vs 2WD all come from the operator's manual and the implement; a wrong number is a re-ballast, not a failure.

assumptions.name: Ratio by task
assumptions.value: ~120-145 lb/hp field draft; ~90-110 lb/hp higher-speed transport; user-supplied

assumptions.name: Slip target
assumptions.value: aim for 8-15% wheel slip; too much ballast wastes fuel, too little spins the tires

haze-machine-sizing.formula: ventilation_cfm = volume_cf x ach / 60; scaling_factor = (volume_cf x ach) / (ref_volume_cf x ref_ach); required_output = ref_output x scaling_factor; time_constant_hr = 1 / ach; time_to_90_hr = ln(10) / ach.
haze-machine-sizing.edition: Haze density as the steady state between machine output and ventilation removal, scaled on the product of volume and air-change rate, with the first-order fill time constant 1/ACH, by name; public mass-balance physics. The machine manufacturer's rated output, the fluid's safety data sheet, and the venue's smoke-detection and fire-authority requirements govern.
haze-machine-sizing.freeAccess: The steady-state mass balance and its exponential approach are public physics. The venue volume, air-change rate, and the reference machine's performance are the user's own values.
haze-machine-sizing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
haze-machine-sizing.editionNote: A hazed room is a steady state, not a fill. The machine adds haze continuously while the ventilation removes it continuously, and the density settles where the two rates match, which makes the required output proportional to the product of volume and air-change rate rather than to volume alone. Double the room and the requirement doubles; leave the room the same size and double the air handlers and the requirement doubles again. Crews consistently size on volume alone and are then surprised when the look will not hold once the HVAC comes on for the audience. The time constant is the other half of the answer and it governs the schedule rather than the equipment. At four air changes per hour a room reaches sixty-three percent of its final density in fifteen minutes and ninety percent in about thirty-five, so a haze cue called two minutes before the top of the show does nothing and the machine has to have been running through the pre-show. At one air change per hour the same room takes over two hours to settle, which is why a tight room hazes beautifully and then will not clear for the next act. Negotiating a lower air-change rate with the building engineer halves the fluid requirement and doubles the fill time, and it is frequently worth more than a second machine.

assumptions.name: Steady state
assumptions.value: required output scales on the PRODUCT of volume and air-change rate, not on volume alone

assumptions.name: Fill time
assumptions.value: first-order approach: 63% of steady state at 1/ACH hours, 90% at ln(10)/ACH

assumptions.name: Governing authority
assumptions.value: the machine's rated output, the fluid's safety data sheet, and the venue's smoke-detection and fire-authority requirements govern

spearman-rank-correlation.formula: Spearman rho = Pearson r on the ranks of x and y (ties take the average rank). Two-sided test for rho = 0: t = rho * sqrt(n - 2) / sqrt(1 - rho^2) on n - 2 df; p = 2 * (1 - tcdf(|t|, n - 2)).
spearman-rank-correlation.edition: OpenIntro Statistics 4th ed. (nonparametric association / rank correlation) by name; the Student-t CDF via the regularized incomplete beta function per Numerical Recipes in C 2nd ed. §6.4. Verified against scipy.stats.spearmanr.
spearman-rank-correlation.freeAccess: OpenIntro Statistics free at openintro.org; Numerical Recipes chapters free at numerical.recipes.
spearman-rank-correlation.governance: Estimate only. Readability formulas and similar metrics are derived from a representative population and have known edge-case noise. The classroom teacher governs final text selection, grade placement, and assessment decisions.
spearman-rank-correlation.editionNote: Spearman's rho is Pearson's r applied to the ranks rather than the raw values, so it captures any monotonic relationship (not just linear) and resists outliers and non-normality - the right measure for ordinal data or a curved but steadily-rising trend. Tied values receive the average of the ranks they span. The two-sided p-value uses the t approximation t = rho sqrt((n-2)/(1-rho^2)) on n-2 df, matching scipy.stats.spearmanr; for very small samples it is only approximate (an exact permutation test is preferred). A perfect monotonic relationship (rho = +/-1) makes the t-statistic unbounded and is reported as a perfect-fit flag with p = 0, never a non-finite field.

assumptions.name: Rank transform
assumptions.value: rho = Pearson r on average-tied ranks of both series

assumptions.name: Two-sided p-value
assumptions.value: t = rho sqrt((n-2)/(1-rho^2)) on n-2 df; p = 2(1 - tcdf(|t|, n-2))

assumptions.name: Scope
assumptions.value: monotonic (not linear) association; small-n p-value is approximate; perfect fit flagged, not left non-finite

compound-curve.formula: T1 = R1 tan(delta1/2); T2 = R2 tan(delta2/2); L = R delta_rad; back tangent t1 = T1 + (T1+T2) sin(delta2)/sin(delta); forward tangent t2 = T2 + (T1+T2) sin(delta1)/sin(delta); delta = delta1 + delta2.
compound-curve.edition: Compound circular-curve geometry per the AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (the Green Book) and Ghilani & Wolf, Elementary Surveying, by name; first-principles trig with the law of sines.
compound-curve.freeAccess: The compound-curve tangent geometry (semi-tangents and the law-of-sines vertex triangle) is standard published route-surveying math; the design of record and the engineer of record govern the alignment.
compound-curve.governance: Estimate. Engineer of record governs the design and acceptance. Verify against the project structural drawings and the manufacturer's published capacity / chart.
compound-curve.editionNote: A compound circular curve: two circular arcs of different radii turning the same direction and meeting at a point of compound curvature (PCC), the geometry of an interchange ramp or an intersection curb return where one radius eases into another. Each arc has its own semi-tangent T = R tan(delta/2) and arc length L = R delta (radians); the common tangent at the PCC has length T1 + T2. The tangent distances back to the point of intersection (PI) of the two outer tangents come from the law of sines on the vertex triangle: the back tangent (PI to the PC) t1 = T1 + (T1 + T2) sin(delta2)/sin(delta), and the forward tangent (PI to the PT) t2 = T2 + (T1 + T2) sin(delta1)/sin(delta), with delta = delta1 + delta2. With equal radii and equal central angles this reduces exactly to the simple circular curve. The two arcs must turn the same direction (a reverse curve is a separate case), and AASHTO limits the ratio of successive compound radii to about 1.5:1 on the mainline to keep the steering change gradual. A design aid; AASHTO and the engineer of record govern.

assumptions.name: Semi-tangents and lengths
assumptions.value: T = R tan(delta/2); L = R delta_rad per arc

assumptions.name: PI tangents
assumptions.value: t1 = T1 + (T1+T2) sin(delta2)/sin(delta); t2 = T2 + (T1+T2) sin(delta1)/sin(delta)
assumptions.source: law of sines on the vertex triangle

assumptions.name: Scope
assumptions.value: same-direction arcs (not a reverse curve); reduces to a simple curve at equal radii/angles

fillet-weld-strength.formula: Effective throat a = 0.707*leg (equal-leg). ASD allowable shear 0.30*F_Exx; LRFD design 0.75*0.60*F_Exx. Capacity = stress * a * length. AISC min fillet (Table J2.4 by thinner part); max (J2.2b) = t - 1/16 for t >= 1/4. Size-from-load solves the leg for a target load.
fillet-weld-strength.edition: Fillet-weld effective throat (0.707*leg) and shear strength (allowable 0.30*F_Exx; LRFD 0.75*0.60*F_Exx) per AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code - Steel and AISC 360 §J2, by name, with the minimum/maximum fillet sizes of AISC Table J2.4 and §J2.2b.
fillet-weld-strength.freeAccess: First-principles weld mechanics. The qualified WPS, the weld inspector, and the engineer of record govern; base-metal and matching-filler checks are the engineer's.
fillet-weld-strength.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed structural engineer govern.
fillet-weld-strength.editionNote: AWS D1.1 / AISC 360 §J2. The ASD/LRFD method is a labeled toggle so the two safety bases are never mixed. Cross-links weld-heat-input and metal-weight.

assumptions.name: Electrode strength
assumptions.value: E60/E70/E80 sets F_Exx; matching filler is the engineer's

shrink-fit.formula: Required temperature change delta_T = (interference + assembly clearance) / (alpha x nominal diameter); heat the outer/bore part to ambient + delta_T, or chill the inner/shaft part to ambient - delta_T. From delta_dia = alpha x dia x delta_T.
shrink-fit.edition: Interference shrink-fit assembly temperature - first-principles thermal-expansion relation delta_dia = alpha x dia x delta_T (steel alpha 6.5e-6 per degF), by name; public domain.
shrink-fit.freeAccess: Pure thermal-expansion arithmetic, public; the diameter, interference, clearance, coefficient, and ambient are user-supplied.
shrink-fit.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
shrink-fit.editionNote: First-principles thermal-growth relation. The alloy's published coefficient governs the number (steel about 6.5e-6 per degF; aluminum and others differ); the interference contact pressure (a separate Lame thick-cylinder analysis) and the engineer govern the joint's holding capacity -- this tile sizes only the assembly temperature.

assumptions.name: Coefficient of thermal expansion
assumptions.value: default 6.5e-6 per degF (steel); editable for the alloy

assumptions.name: Ambient
assumptions.value: default 70 degF; a chill below dry ice (-109 degF) needs liquid nitrogen

tolerance-stack-rss.formula: tol_wc = sum(|tol_i|); tol_rss = sqrt(sum(tol_i^2)); gap = nominal +/- tol.
tolerance-stack-rss.edition: Worst-case and RSS (root-sum-square) tolerance stack-up, standard mechanical-design / GD&T practice, by name.
tolerance-stack-rss.freeAccess: The worst-case sum and the RSS square-root-of-sum-of-squares are public tolerance-analysis results.
tolerance-stack-rss.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
tolerance-stack-rss.editionNote: Tolerance stack-up on a dimension chain: the worst-case tolerance is the arithmetic sum of the individual half-widths (a fit always achieved but often overbuilt), while the statistical RSS tolerance is the square root of the sum of the squares - the realistic assembly spread when the dimensions vary independently, are centered on nominal, and are roughly normally distributed. RSS is never looser than worst-case (equal for a single dimension), and the gap between them widens as the chain lengthens. This returns both tolerances and the resulting fits; it assumes centered, independent, normal dimensions (add a static offset or a Cpk factor for a shifted process). A design aid; the drawing tolerances and the assembly's criticality govern.

assumptions.name: Worst-case
assumptions.value: tol_wc = sum of the half-widths

assumptions.name: RSS
assumptions.value: tol_rss = sqrt(sum of squares)

assumptions.name: RSS assumptions
assumptions.value: centered, independent, normally distributed dimensions

pool-alkalinity-adjust.formula: Raise: ~1.5 lb sodium bicarbonate per 10,000 gal per 10 ppm; lower: ~25 fl oz of 31.45% (20 Baume) muriatic acid per 10,000 gal per 10 ppm.
pool-alkalinity-adjust.edition: NSPF CPO Handbook / ANSI-APSP-ICC dosing tables (by name).
pool-alkalinity-adjust.freeAccess: Product labels and SDS free with the chemical; CPO course materials proprietary.
pool-alkalinity-adjust.governance: Math aid for personal verification. Stop work and consult the qualified person on site if any number does not match the field condition.
pool-alkalinity-adjust.editionNote: Single-edition (engineering-practice / first-principles take-off; refresh as practice and product data shift).

assumptions.name: Target TA band
assumptions.value: ~80-120 ppm (advisory; lower for salt/plaster, higher for vinyl)

engine-fuel-burn-gph.formula: gph = horsepower x bsfc / fuel_density; run_hours = tank / gph; diesel ~7.1 lb/gal, gasoline ~6.1 lb/gal.
engine-fuel-burn-gph.edition: Brake-specific fuel consumption (BSFC) fuel-flow relation, standard engine-performance practice by name; first-principles mass-to-volume conversion.
engine-fuel-burn-gph.freeAccess: The BSFC fuel-flow relation (lb/hr = HP x BSFC) and fuel densities are standard published engine-performance results.
engine-fuel-burn-gph.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
engine-fuel-burn-gph.editionNote: Brake-specific fuel consumption (BSFC) is the pounds of fuel an engine burns per horsepower per hour, so the fuel mass flow = horsepower x BSFC and the volume flow (gph) = that divided by the fuel density (diesel about 7.1 lb/gal, gasoline about 6.1). A modern diesel runs BSFC roughly 0.35-0.40 near its efficient load; a naturally aspirated gasoline engine roughly 0.45-0.55, so for the same power a gasoline engine burns markedly more volume per hour. Given a tank size, run time = tank / gph. This is the burn at the entered power (usually near-full); the real burn over a duty cycle with part-load operation is lower. A planning aid; the engine's published fuel map and a measured burn govern.

assumptions.name: BSFC flow
assumptions.value: lb/hr = HP x BSFC; gph = lb/hr / fuel density

assumptions.name: Fuel density
assumptions.value: diesel ~7.1 lb/gal, gasoline ~6.1 lb/gal

assumptions.name: Full-power burn
assumptions.value: the burn at the entered power; part-load duty-cycle burn is lower

waterline-for-hull-speed.formula: waterline_length_ft = (target_hull_speed_kn / coefficient)^2, the displacement hull-speed relation hull_speed = 1.34 x sqrt(LWL) solved for the waterline; coefficient default 1.34.
waterline-for-hull-speed.edition: Displacement hull-speed relation (Froude speed-length theory), solved for the waterline, by name; the actual hull form, displacement, and power govern.
waterline-for-hull-speed.freeAccess: The speed-length relation is a published empirical result of displacement-hull / Froude theory.
waterline-for-hull-speed.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
waterline-for-hull-speed.editionNote: The inverse of hull-speed: the waterline a PURE DISPLACEMENT hull needs to reach a target speed without climbing its own bow wave. Near the speed-length ratio of 1.34 the bow and stern waves merge and the hull hits a practical wall, so this is the displacement ceiling, not a hard limit - a semi-displacement or planing hull exceeds it with enough power and the right form. The coefficient is an approximation (some references use 1.34 to 1.4, editable). A planning estimate; the hull form, displacement, and power govern.

assumptions.name: Displacement wall
assumptions.value: LWL = (speed / 1.34)^2 is the waterline for the displacement ceiling

assumptions.name: Approximation
assumptions.value: the coefficient varies 1.34 to 1.4; a planing hull breaks the ceiling

cutting-fluid-concentration.formula: Concentration % = Brix x refractometer factor; add concentrate = sump x (target - current) / (100 - target); add water = sump x (current - target) / target.
cutting-fluid-concentration.freeAccess: Refractometer factor and the maintenance range free on the coolant data sheet.
cutting-fluid-concentration.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
cutting-fluid-concentration.editionNote: Single-edition (engineering-practice / first-principles take-off; refresh as practice and product data shift).

assumptions.name: Maintenance range
assumptions.value: often ~6-10% for general machining; factor usually 1-4 (off the data sheet)

hvac-equipment-circuit.formula: MCA = 1.25 x largest motor RLA + sum of the other loads (NEC 440.33). MOCP = 1.75 x largest RLA + others, taken to the next NEC 240.6(A) standard size DOWN (NEC 440.22(A)); the 225% value is the ceiling allowed only where the 175% size will not start the equipment.
hvac-equipment-circuit.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed electrician govern. Verify against the NEC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
hvac-equipment-circuit.editionNote: Single-edition (verify the NEC edition adopted by your AHJ; the equipment nameplate's stamped MCA/MOCP governs).

assumptions.name: RLA basis
assumptions.value: the largest motor's rated-load amps (RLA), not locked-rotor amps (LRA); the compressor is normally the largest

assumptions.name: MOCP rounding
assumptions.value: 175% is a ceiling, so the device is the largest NEC 240.6(A) standard size not exceeding it (round down); 225% only if needed to start

assumptions.name: Conductor
assumptions.value: the branch-circuit conductor ampacity must be at least the MCA

wind-cc-pressure.formula: qh = 0.00256 Kz Kzt Kd Ke V^2; p_a = qh (GCp - GCpi); p_b = qh (GCp + GCpi); governing = the larger magnitude of p_a, p_b.
wind-cc-pressure.edition: The ASCE 7-22 Chapter 30 components-and-cladding design pressure p = qh [(GCp) - (GCpi)], with the velocity pressure qh = 0.00256 Kz Kzt Kd Ke V^2 (Kd = 0.85, V in mph) and GCpi = +/-0.18 for an enclosed building, by name; GCp is read from the Chapter 30 zone figures.
wind-cc-pressure.freeAccess: ASCE 7 is available through the ASCE Library at ascelibrary.org; the Chapter 30 C&C provisions and the 0.00256 velocity-pressure constant are public.
wind-cc-pressure.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
wind-cc-pressure.editionNote: The ASCE 7-22 Chapter 30 C&C design pressure p = qh [(GCp) - (GCpi)], the velocity pressure qh = 0.00256 Kz Kzt Kd Ke V^2 with Kd = 0.85 and GCpi = +/-0.18 (enclosed), and GCp read from the Chapter 30 figures for the zone and effective wind area. This returns the C&C design pressure for an entered GCp and the computed qh - it does not read the zone figures for the user (enter GCp for the roof/wall zone and effective wind area), assumes an enclosed building unless GCpi is changed, and does not cover the MWFRS pressures (wind-mwfrs-pressure) or the parapet/overhang special cases. A design aid, not a substitute for the structural engineer of record's stamped design.

assumptions.name: Velocity pressure
assumptions.value: qh = 0.00256 Kz Kzt Kd Ke V^2 at mean roof height (Kd = 0.85, V in mph)

assumptions.name: Design pressure
assumptions.value: p = qh (GCp - GCpi); both internal signs evaluated, the larger magnitude governs

assumptions.name: GCp
assumptions.value: read from the Chapter 30 zone figures by roof/wall zone and effective wind area (entered)

wall-condensation-gradient.formula: R_total = R_inside + R_outside; T_plane = T_in - (R_inside/R_total)(T_in - T_out); T_dew = Magnus(T_in, RH); margin = T_plane - T_dew (<= 0 condensing).
wall-condensation-gradient.edition: The R-proportional through-wall temperature gradient and the Magnus dew-point comparison for a condensation-plane screen, standard building-science results, by name.
wall-condensation-gradient.freeAccess: The R-proportional gradient and the Magnus dew-point approximation are public building-science results.
wall-condensation-gradient.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
wall-condensation-gradient.editionNote: The interface temperature T_plane = T_in - (R_inside/R_total)(T_in - T_out), the Magnus dew-point approximation for the indoor air, and the condensation criterion T_plane <= T_dew. This returns the condensation-plane temperature and its margin to the dew point - it is a one-dimensional steady-state thermal gradient (no thermal bridging, air movement, or vapor-diffusion/transient moisture accumulation, which a Glaser or hygrothermal model adds), uses the interior air's dew point (moderated by any vapor retarder), and is a screen. A building-science aid, not a substitute for a hygrothermal (WUFI-type) analysis; the assembly's vapor control and a full moisture analysis govern.

assumptions.name: Temperature gradient
assumptions.value: T_plane = T_in - (R_inside/R_total)(T_in - T_out), 1-D steady state

assumptions.name: Dew point
assumptions.value: Magnus approximation of the indoor air's dew point

assumptions.name: Screen only
assumptions.value: no vapor diffusion or transient moisture; a Glaser/WUFI model is more complete

rc-slab-max-span-for-thickness.formula: max_span = available_thickness x denom / (12 x kfy x klw), the ACI 318-19 minimum-thickness relation hmin = 12 l / denom x kfy x klw solved for the span; denom = {simply:20, one-end:24, both-ends:28, cantilever:10}.
rc-slab-max-span-for-thickness.edition: The ACI 318-19 Table 7.3.1.1 (one-way slabs) and Table 9.3.1.1 (beams) minimum thickness for deflection control, solved for the span, with the (0.4 + fy/100,000) non-Grade-60 modifier and the lightweight-concrete factor, by name.
rc-slab-max-span-for-thickness.freeAccess: ACI 318 is readable free through the ACI online reading room at concrete.org; the minimum-thickness tables are in the published code.
rc-slab-max-span-for-thickness.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
rc-slab-max-span-for-thickness.editionNote: The inverse of rc-slab-min-thickness: with the depth fixed, the longest span that still waives an explicit deflection calculation. A longer span needs a deflection calculation or a deeper member. It applies to normalweight (unless wc is set) members not supporting or attached to partitions or construction likely to be damaged by large deflections, uses the clear span, and is not the strength (flexure/shear) design. A design aid, not a substitute for the structural engineer of record's stamped design.

assumptions.name: Span from depth
assumptions.value: max_span = h x denom / (12 kfy klw), the minimum-thickness table inverted

assumptions.name: Grade modifier
assumptions.value: (0.4 + fy/100,000) for fy other than 60,000 psi

assumptions.name: Scope
assumptions.value: members not supporting partitions likely to be damaged by deflection; not a strength design

rc-beam-flexure.formula: a = As x fy / (0.85 x f'c x b); Mn = As x fy x (d - a/2); phi Mn = 0.90 x Mn (tension-controlled); util = Mu / phi Mn.
rc-beam-flexure.edition: ACI 318-19 (Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete), by name: §22.2.2.4.1 (equivalent rectangular stress block), §22.2 (nominal flexural strength), §21.2.2 (phi = 0.90 tension-controlled).
rc-beam-flexure.freeAccess: ACI 318-19 is viewable through ACI's online public-access reader; the stress-block and moment-arm arithmetic is public and printed in every reinforced-concrete text.
rc-beam-flexure.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
rc-beam-flexure.editionNote: ACI 318-19 §22.2.2.4.1 (equivalent rectangular stress block, a = As x fy / (0.85 x f'c x b)), §22.2 (Mn = As x fy x (d - a/2)), and §21.2.2 (the strength-reduction factor phi = 0.90 for a tension-controlled section). fy defaults to 60,000 psi (Grade 60, the standard deformed-bar grade). Covers only a singly-reinforced rectangular section assumed tension-controlled - the user must confirm the net tensile strain epsilon_t is at least 0.005 (§21.2.2), and compression reinforcement, T-beam flange action, minimum steel (§9.6.1.2), and shear (see rc-beam-shear) are not checked here. Take As and d from the reinforcement schedule for the actual section. A design aid, not a substitute for a licensed engineer's design - the engineer of record's stamped design governs.

assumptions.name: Section basis
assumptions.value: singly-reinforced rectangular section, tension-controlled (epsilon_t >= 0.005, phi = 0.90); confirm the strain, and use a doubly-reinforced or T-beam analysis where the section calls for it

assumptions.name: Grade 60 default
assumptions.value: fy defaults to 60,000 psi (Grade 60 deformed bar), editable for Gr 40 / Gr 80

assumptions.name: Companion checks separate
assumptions.value: minimum steel (§9.6.1.2), shear (rc-beam-shear), deflection, and development (rc-development-length) are separate checks

consolidation-degree.edition: Terzaghi one-dimensional consolidation theory (time factor Tv), inverted for U, as compiled in Das, Principles of Geotechnical Engineering, by name.
consolidation-degree.freeAccess: The Terzaghi time-factor series and the Tv = cv t/Hdr^2 relation are standard published soil-mechanics results.
consolidation-degree.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
consolidation-degree.editionNote: The inverse of the consolidation-time tile: the degree of consolidation U reached after an elapsed time t, from the dimensionless time factor Tv = cv t / Hdr^2 inverted through Terzaghi's two-branch series - U = 100 sqrt(4 Tv / pi) for Tv <= 0.283 (U <= 60%) and U = 100 - 10^((1.781 - Tv)/0.933) above. The drainage path Hdr is the longest distance water travels to a drainage boundary - the full clay-layer thickness for single (one-way) drainage or half for double (two-way) drainage - so mis-identifying it changes Tv by a factor of four. Because the consolidation decelerates, U approaches 100% asymptotically and never quite reaches it. This returns Tv and U; it does not compute the settlement magnitude (see the settlement tiles) or secondary compression. A design aid; the engineer of record and the site-specific cv from an oedometer test govern.

assumptions.name: Time factor
assumptions.value: Tv = cv t / Hdr^2

assumptions.name: Drainage path
assumptions.value: Hdr = full layer (single) or half (double drainage)

carburizing-case-depth.formula: the parabolic diffusion relation case depth = k x sqrt(time), inverted as time = (depth / k)^2, so doubling a case QUADRUPLES the cycle.
carburizing-case-depth.edition: Carburising case depth kinetics. The rate constant k is taken from an ENTERED reference case -- a depth this furnace reached in a known time, k = depth / sqrt(time) -- because it depends strongly on carburising temperature, on the atmosphere's carbon potential and on the steel, and a published figure for one combination does not transfer to another.
carburizing-case-depth.freeAccess: One diffusion relation fixed by an entered reference case.
carburizing-case-depth.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
carburizing-case-depth.editionNote: Depth goes with the SQUARE ROOT of time, so a deeper case costs far more than it looks: doubling a case quadruples the cycle, which on a batch furnace is the difference between two loads a day and one every two days. The temperature lever is real and not free -- raising the carburising temperature increases k substantially and reaches the same case in far less time, at the cost of grain coarsening, more distortion to correct in grinding, and shorter fixture and furnace life. AND THE SPECIFICATION TRAP IS WHERE SUPPLIER AND CUSTOMER DISAGREE ABOUT A CORRECT PART: 'case depth 0.030 in' does not say whether it is EFFECTIVE case depth measured to a stated hardness or TOTAL case depth, and the total is always larger.

assumptions.name: Reference case is entered
assumptions.value: k = reference depth / sqrt(reference time); it depends on temperature, atmosphere and steel

assumptions.name: Effective and total case differ
assumptions.value: and the drawing must say which, and to what hardness

assumptions.name: Hardness profile is not predicted
assumptions.value: it depends on the quench as much as on the carburising

zonal-pressure-diagnostics.formula: pressure ratio = zone pressure with reference to outdoors / house pressure with reference to outdoors, both taken during a blower door depressurization; the ratio of the two series leakage paths follows as (ratio / (1 - ratio))^n on the field flow exponent n = 0.65 (Energy Conservatory; JLC 2023).
zonal-pressure-diagnostics.edition: The zonal pressure diagnostic as building-performance field practice states it, with the series-leakage interpretation on the field flow exponent n = 0.65. It is a RATIO diagnostic: it says which of two planes is leakier, not how many cfm either passes.
zonal-pressure-diagnostics.freeAccess: One measured ratio and one 0.65-power relation.
zonal-pressure-diagnostics.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
zonal-pressure-diagnostics.editionNote: A ratio near the house pressure means the plane between the house and the zone is the leaky one and the zone is effectively inside; a ratio near zero means that plane is tight and the zone is effectively outdoors. That single reading decides where the money goes, and it is the answer to the question a blower door number cannot address at all -- an attic at house pressure is being ventilated by the house, and insulating over it without air sealing first is close to wasted work.

assumptions.name: Flow exponent 0.65
assumptions.value: real envelopes run roughly 0.5 to 0.75

assumptions.name: Series leakage, two planes
assumptions.value: a zone with a third path is not this model

assumptions.name: A ratio, not a flow
assumptions.value: it does not report cfm through either plane; zonal-add-a-hole does, from an add-a-hole test

condenser-td-head-pressure.formula: condensing temperature = ambient on the correct basis + TD; the change between two cases is that difference, and the compressor power change is that difference times the entered percent per degF; annual energy = compressor kW x that percent x hours, at 0.745699872 kW/hp.
condenser-td-head-pressure.edition: Condensing temperature = ambient + TD as condenser practice writes it, with the basis distinction ASHRAE Refrigeration states: air-cooled TD from the DRY bulb, evaporative TD from the WET bulb. The compressor power sensitivity is ENTERED (commonly one and a half to two percent per degF) because it depends on refrigerant, suction condition and machine. It does not size the condenser, compute the heat of rejection, or look up saturation pressure.
condenser-td-head-pressure.freeAccess: One sum, one difference, and one entered sensitivity.
condenser-td-head-pressure.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
condenser-td-head-pressure.editionNote: The basis is the part most often got wrong. An air-cooled condenser's TD is measured from the dry bulb and an evaporative condenser's from the wet bulb, which in most US summers runs well below it -- so an evaporative unit at a wider TD can still condense cooler than an air-cooled unit at a tighter one, and reading a TD against the wrong basis produces a diagnosis off by the entire wet-bulb depression. Capacity is roughly linear in TD but compressor power responds to condensing TEMPERATURE, so adding surface until the TD drops a few degrees cuts power continuously for the life of the plant.

assumptions.name: The basis is selected, not inferred
assumptions.value: air-cooled from dry bulb, evaporative from wet bulb

assumptions.name: The power sensitivity is entered
assumptions.value: it depends on refrigerant, suction condition and compressor

assumptions.name: It does not size the condenser
assumptions.value: the manufacturer's rated capacity at the design condition governs

umbilical-air-supply.formula: required surface flow (scfm) = the rate per diver (acfm) x the absolute pressure (1 + depth / 33 seawater) x the number of divers including the standby; the deepest compliant depth = 33 x (compressor capacity / (rate x divers) - 1); the volume tank's usable gas = its capacity x (its pressure - the bottom pressure, depth x 14.7 / 33) / 14.7 psi, before the helmet's over-bottom pressure.
umbilical-air-supply.edition: The surface-supplied flow relation by name, with the independent reserve breathing supply named as a SEPARATE regulatory requirement. The rate per diver is set by the applicable regulation, not by arithmetic. The applicable commercial diving regulations, the operation's diving safety manual, and the diving supervisor govern.
umbilical-air-supply.freeAccess: Flow arithmetic on the spread's own equipment figures; no regulatory table is reproduced.
umbilical-air-supply.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
umbilical-air-supply.editionNote: The requirement scales with absolute pressure exactly as a scuba diver's does, so a compressor sized for shallow work falls short in deeper water with no change in the number of divers and no warning that anything has changed. The diver count multiplies it directly and the standby diver counts -- a spread sized for the divers in the water is undersized. The reserve is regulatory rather than engineering and is a separate calculation from the flow: surface-supplied diving requires an independent reserve breathing supply, sized to bring the diver to the surface from the maximum depth including any required decompression, and available without the diver having to do anything to switch to it. A volume tank that meets the flow requirement but not the reserve requirement does not comply, so both margins are reported and passing one is not passing. The useful output for a supervisor is the depth at which the spread stops meeting the requirement, because that is the limit that otherwise gets discovered at the dive station.

assumptions.name: The standby diver counts
assumptions.value: a spread sized for the divers in the water is undersized

assumptions.name: Reserve is separate from flow
assumptions.value: meeting one requirement is not meeting the other

assumptions.name: The rate per diver is regulatory
assumptions.value: it depends on jurisdiction, mode of diving, and depth

dock-door-count-throughput.formula: Door-hours = trucks x turn time; doors at full utilisation = door-hours / operating hours; doors required = that count / practical utilisation, rounded up; the peak is computed the same way over the peak window.
dock-door-count-throughput.edition: The facility's own arrival data, turn-time measurement, and yard and detention practice.
dock-door-count-throughput.freeAccess: Queueing arithmetic only; no purchased standard is required to reproduce it.
dock-door-count-throughput.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
dock-door-count-throughput.editionNote: Turn time is the whole time a trailer occupies the door -- spotting, securing, handling, counting and paperwork, and release. A dock measuring handling time and calling it turn time will be short of doors by the difference.

assumptions.name: Practical utilisation
assumptions.value: 60 to 70% is the ordinary planning range; utilisation below 100% is not slack but what makes the dock work
assumptions.source: industry practice, entered as an input

assumptions.name: Peak
assumptions.value: a share of arrivals in a stated window; sizing on the daily average understates the requirement by the peaking factor

well-decline-reserves.formula: exponential decline q(t) = q_i exp(-Dt); cumulative N = (q_i - q)/D; economic life t = ln(q_i/q_econ)/D; effective annual decline = 1 - exp(-D).
well-decline-reserves.edition: Exponential decline only. Unconventional wells decline hyperbolically and this says so rather than fitting them.
well-decline-reserves.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
well-decline-reserves.editionNote: TWO FORMS OF THE SAME NUMBER CIRCULATE AND GET CONFUSED: the nominal decline that goes in the exponent, and the effective annual decline that people quote as 'a 28% decline'. The well here declines 0.28 nominal, which is 24.4% effective -- and someone who reads the same 28% as effective computes a nominal of 0.329, an economic life of 10.1 years instead of 11.9, and 450,000 barrels instead of 528,000. That is 15% low on one well and material on a package. Both readings are reported here from the one number entered, because which of the two a quoted decline is meant to be is exactly what nobody writes down. THE PRACTICAL OUTPUT IS THE DATE RATHER THAN THE BARRELS: a well is abandoned when its rate stops covering lease operating expense, and plugging liability, equipment redeployment and workover decisions are all scheduled from that year. AND EXPONENTIAL IS THE WRONG MODEL FOR A SHALE WELL, where an exponential fit on early data dramatically understates reserves and a high-b hyperbolic fit far into the future overstates them.

assumptions.name: Exponential decline only
assumptions.value: unconventional wells are hyperbolic and need a b factor and a terminal decline

assumptions.name: Constant economic limit
assumptions.value: the limit moves with price and with operating cost

assumptions.name: Not a reserves estimate
assumptions.value: no classification standard is applied

refrigeration-outage-holdover.formula: Q = U x A x (T_ambient - T_box) x (1 + infiltration allowance), or the entered closed-door gain; E = product lb x cp x (T_allowable - T_start); holdover = E / Q; dry ice = Q / 246 lb/h, and for an outage of T hours max(0, Q x T - E) / 246 lb; USDA check 50 x 246 / 48 = 256 Btu/h.
refrigeration-outage-holdover.edition: An energy balance by name, with the FDA Food Code Section 3-501.16 cold-holding limit (41 degF) and the USDA FSIS power-outage guidance (about 4 hours for an unopened refrigerator; a full freezer about 48 hours, half full about 24; 50 lb of dry ice holds a full 18 cu ft freezer about 2 days) cited as the limit and the check, and dry ice's heat of sublimation, about 246 Btu/lb, as physical data.
refrigeration-outage-holdover.freeAccess: The FDA Food Code is free at fda.gov and the USDA FSIS power-outage guidance is free at fsis.usda.gov; the arithmetic runs on the user's own box, product, and temperatures.
refrigeration-outage-holdover.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed mechanical contractor govern. ACCA Manual J / D / S supersede rules of thumb.
refrigeration-outage-holdover.editionNote: A cooler without power warms at the rate heat leaks in, and the product is what slows it. The allowable rise is what makes holdover shorter than people expect: a box at 35 degF has six degrees before the 41 degF cold-holding limit, so a full box buys less time than its weight suggests. The tile leaves out door openings, and every opening dumps the cold air, so keeping the door shut is worth more than any other action. The closed-door allowance is applied only when the gain is built from the box; an entered gain is taken as the whole closed-door gain. The USDA household figure implies a leak of about 256 Btu/h in a full 18 cu ft freezer, reported as an order-of-magnitude check on the method. Dry ice gives off carbon dioxide and must not be used in an unventilated occupied space. Whether product that has been out of temperature is safe is the food safety or pharmacy authority's decision, and pharmaceutical storage has its own limits.
